title: USBLL: Reassemble transactions into transfers
description:
Create pseudo URB and pass the reassembled data to USB URB dissector.
Reassembly for control transfers is not problematic as the transfer
length is known. For bulk transfers assume the transfer can span across
multiple transactions, however for periodic (interrupt and isochronous)
assume the transfer never spans across multiple transactions.
    
Rely on USB dissector to provide endpoint maximum packet size. Actual
interface/configuration handling in USB dissector needs to be reworked
as the code assumes that there is only one configuration and alternate
interface configurations have matching endpoints.
    
While the reassembly bulk transfers and never reassemble periodic
transfers result in pretty good dissection, the USB class dissectors
need a mechanism to provide transfer size hints to USBLL dissector.
Such hint is not needed for software USB capture as software sniffers
essentially capture URBs and every transfer is associated with one URB.
The problem can be seen for example in Mass Storage Class where it is
common for data transfers length to be multiple of endpoint maximum
packet size. Because USBLL dissector doesn't know expected transfer
size, it combines together data and status transport.

Related to #15908

added 1 commit
  • 57d91756 - [WIP] USBLL: Reassemble control transfers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2848/diffs?diff_id=179897505&start_sha=96bcb60e57fe1869f72c7bc0d9eaf0104576426c)

I am not so sure about suitability of the generic reassembly code here. USB transfers are always ordered and in case of retransmission, the data should match. I am not sure about the multiple tails - is it going to trigger here if the last data packet gets retransmitted?

While I think it would be nice to have custom reassembly that would take into account USB retransmission rules, using generic reassembly is perfectly fine in majority of cases. As this is already quite large change, I think it is best to merge this using the generic reassembly code.

Most likely the processing needs to happen in usbll dissector. This is because the information is already needed before reassembly. Endpoint 0 maximum packet size is 8, 16, 32 or 64, and as such always the first 8 bytes of DEVICE descriptor will be in first data packet (the 8th byte contains the maximum packet size).

changed this line in [version 5 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2848/diffs?diff_id=216742075&start_sha=3c3eacf36f1a114bc5b46430219377cd18b49557#2a2aed97fb4c277c1e3f572e7b1e265ae1b55a72_1298_1356)
changed the description
For the time being that's probably the best thing to do, but should we eventually separate URB from actual USB transfer? Such separation would actually make sense for both USBLL and MAUSB.

added 1 commit
  • 1bf267f0 - [WIP] USBLL: Reassemble control transfers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/2848/diffs?diff_id=180253561&start_sha=57d91756bd689eaef2fbb0fd13faa04447131b87)

While this makes the control transfers reassembly working for low speed devices, it is pretty much misplaced. It would be nice to have such information at hand when reassembling other transfers (e.g. bulk), but it is seriously complicated to fill the value here for other endpoints (handling it for ep0 is already an ugly hack). To obtain the max packet size for other endpoints we have to keep track of active configuration and interface settings.

This seems not bad after all. The actual tracking has to be implemented in USB dissector (so we don't duplicate logic). Current implementation is not so nice, but it works. To implement it cleanly the actual configuration/interface handling code has to be reworked.
